note: Wednesday run, 23 Sep 2026 SGT. Latest completed cash sessions: US/HK/SGX closed Tue 22 Sep; JPX remains shut through Wed for a bank holiday (Nikkei stale to Fri 18 Sep close); KRX/HSI last traded Mon 21 Sep. Tuesday was a genuinely two-sided session that resists a clean risk-on/risk-off label. US equities were flat-to-modestly-higher (S&P500 7,764.6 roughly flat, Nasdaq +0.45% to 27,244, Dow -0.36% to 51,864, Russell2000 +0.51% to 2,890) and VIX fell a further 4.44% to 14.21, even as the 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.8-5.0% (close to cycle highs) and the dollar index sat near a three-month high around 100.4, both still reflecting the Sept 16 FOMC's hawkish dot plot (16 of 19 officials project at least one more 2026 hike; median fed-funds projection 4.1% for both 2026 and 2027; Chair Warsh declined to submit a dot). Oil told a far more dramatic story than equities: WTI collapsed -6.42% to $89.63 while Brent fell a comparatively modest -1.89% to $98.44 (USO -2.75% to $144.08, XLE -1.09%), a US-specific move tied to reports of a large (>7mn bbl) commercial crude stockpile build layering fresh oversupply fears on top of ongoing Strait-of-Hormuz reopening diplomacy. Precious metals and miners are breaking out hard again -- GDX +3.60% to $97.83, SILJ +4.36% to $31.09, SLVP +3.81% to $39.51, SLV +1.84% to $60.73, gold futures +0.37% to $4,400.10 -- a genuine decoupling from the standard real-rate trade (yields and the dollar both firm) that looks more like central-bank buying, Fed-independence anxiety following Trump's removal of Governor Lisa Cook, and geopolitical hedging than a rates-driven rally. All of this unfolds against the Trump-Xi Washington summit (Sept 23-25, main event Sept 24, Xi's first White House visit since 2008), where most analysts expect continuity/stabilization rather than a breakthrough on rare earths or tariffs -- consistent with today's rare-earth basket dispersion (MP +2.08% to $51.04, Lynas +3.79% to $14.51, Energy Fuels -1.30% to $12.14) -- and Bitcoin's quiet -0.49% consolidation just under $86,180, still comfortably above its 50-week moving average. August payrolls (+162k vs +53k consensus, unemployment steady at 4.1%, wages +3.1% y/y) and cooling-but-elevated core CPI (2.4% y/y, headline 3.4%) round out a picture of a resilient economy that gives the Fed cover to stay hawkish without an acute growth scare.

macro.regime: Risk-on cooling -- hawkish-Fed dollar surge triggers a broad, vol-up pullback and a hard reversal in precious metals, while credit stays tight and the Trump-Xi summit outcome remains pending
macro.narrative: Wednesday delivered a broad, volatility-up pullback across almost every risk asset -- S&P -0.76%, Nasdaq -0.69%, Dow -1.03%, Russell2000 -1.28%, VIX +2.08% to 15.18 -- reversing the prior week's vol-compression as a hawkish Fed chorus (Richmond's Barkin said Tuesday 'the risks to inflation outweigh the risks to maximum employment... that's why we raised rates,' calling the economy 'firming') pushed the Dollar Index to roughly 100.70-100.90, its highest since late July. That dollar surge, layered on profit-taking and stop-loss cascades after the metals' multi-day breakout stalled at resistance, drove the sharpest precious-metals reversal of the run: SLV -4.23%, GLD -1.80%, GDX -4.36%, with silver hit doubly hard by fresh concern over softening industrial/solar demand on top of the monetary unwind. Energy fell for an unrelated, idiosyncratic reason: EIA reported a surprise crude build of +2.97M barrels versus a forecast -0.7M draw, sending WTI down 2.58% (Brent's own Sept 23 print is flagged thin-volume/unreliable in the price spine, so no specific Brent close is asserted here) even as the rare-earth basket showed renewed dispersion (MP -4.21% vs LYC.AX +1.10%) ahead of the Trump-Xi summit's main Thursday session in Washington, whose outcome had not yet occurred as of this Singapore-morning writeup. Credit stayed calm throughout the equity wobble -- HY OAS holding near 266-270bp and IG OAS near 77-80bp, both close to cycle-tight levels -- which argues this is a genuine but contained repricing around Fed hawkishness rather than a stress event or a reversal of the broader uptrend.

A genuinely split and now weaker complex: precious metals reversed hard (SLV -4.23%, GDX -4.36%) on dollar strength, profit-taking, and silver-specific industrial-demand worries, while energy fell separately on a surprise EIA crude build (+2.97M vs -0.7M forecast) despite XLE holding up (+0.95%). BTC pulled back to roughly $84,477 (-1.97%), consistent with the broader dollar-driven risk-asset wobble rather than a crypto-specific catalyst; the recent 50-week-MA breakout and short-squeeze technical structure remain intact but leverage risk is a live concern after such a fast prior run.

The hawkish Fed chorus (Barkin, 22 Sep) and Dollar Index's push to a 7-week high signal firming rate expectations, a headwind for duration even though credit spreads (HY ~266-270bp, IG ~77-80bp) remain calm and show no stress. Reintroducing a modest duration headwind after last week's more balanced dot-plot read.

The Dollar Index rallied to its highest level since late July (~100.70-100.90) on reinforced hawkish Fed rhetoric (Barkin: economy 'firming,' inflation risk dominant), directly pressuring gold/silver and providing a genuine near-term case for cash/USD exposure over non-yielding risk assets, pending Thursday's Trump-Xi summit outcome as a swing factor.
